extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, reviewers, journal editors, and open-science advocates (particularly those interested in PLOS publishing and preprints)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples of practices for making peer review more open and transparent (e.g., linking reviewer reports to preprints, publishing peer review histories, reviewer credit). Aimed at journals, editors, authors and reviewers implementing or participating in open peer review pilots and workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness throughout the research process (including peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Openess throughout the research process, including during peer review, is important to not only increase transparency, but to support more flexible and integrated forms of knowledge sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness should be applied across research and evaluation stages to promote transparency and richer scholarly communication; aim to balance accessibility with integrity and appropriate protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review comes in different forms such as signed reviews, publicly available peer review reports and ways of opening the peer review process to a wider pool of experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider which mix of open practices to adopt (e.g., signed vs anonymous, publishing reports, widening reviewer pools) based on discipline norms, author/reviewer preferences, and goals for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking peer review comments to preprints (peer-reviewed preprints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submitting to PLOS Global Public Health can opt in to have their peer review comments posted to their preprint as their manuscript undergoes formal evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking official peer reviewer reports to preprints: (a) enables readers to benefit from expert evaluations earlier; (b) signals when a preprint has undergone peer review, enhancing trust and surfacing the full scholarly conversation. Use opt-in workflows and monitor engagement (e.g., why authors opt in, how readers use reviewed preprints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preprints to accelerate access to expert evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints offer an important pathway for rapid dissemination, especially in fields like global health where timely access to research can have real-world impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair preprint posting with mechanisms that surface expert assessment (e.g., posting reviewer reports) so that early readers can see both the preliminary work and subsequent evaluations; this supports timely uptake while indicating review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published Peer Review History (sharing complete peer review reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing authors to opt in to share their complete peer review reports combining reviewer comments and editorial decisions alongside their published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement opt-in publication of the full peer review history to increase transparency about the editorial process; provide clear presentation of reviewer comments and editorial decisions so readers understand the review trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recognition and credit (signing reviews and ORCID integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support reviewers who wish to sign their reviews, and integrate with tools like ORCID to enable reviewer credit even for anonymous reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mechanisms for reviewer credit (ORCID assertions, signed reviews) while preserving options for anonymity; make crediting easy and interoperable with researcher identifiers to acknowledge reviewer contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of preprint comments in editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage editors to consider preprint comments as part of the peer review process across all our journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should actively monitor and incorporate substantive community feedback on preprints when making editorial decisions, treating preprint commentary as a legitimate source of expert input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable peer review and reuse of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Portable peer review: provide journal-agnostic, high-quality peer review services (e.g., Review Commons) and accept reviews that accompany submissions from other sources to expedite editorial decisions and reduce strain on the reviewer pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt policies and partnerships that allow reuse/transfer of reviews (portable reviews, review exchanges, MetaROR, PCI collaborations) to decrease duplication of reviewer effort and speed decision-making; ensure quality and relevance checks for transferred reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency fosters trust, accountability, efficiency, and richer scholarly dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Open peer review promotes accountability and reduces potential for bias, by making the evaluation process visible. It supports integrity by surfacing the expert assessment that underpins the evaluation of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transparency as a guiding principle when designing review workflows: prioritize measures that increase accountability and reduce bias while maintaining rigorous assessment standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative learning, evaluation, and community engagement for open peer review initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re eager to learn from this pilot: What motivates authors to share their reviews? How do readers engage with peer-reviewed preprints? The answers will help shape the future of how we can support open science beyond the traditional article format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat openness initiatives as pilots to be evaluated: collect data on motivations and reader engagement, solicit community feedback, and iterate on policies to ensure solutions are tailored to author/reviewer needs and maintain integrity.
